To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the presence or absence of cycle-specific events in a synchronous culture can be easily determined; (ii) cycle-specific events can be detected in the presence of cycle-independent events; and (iii) the timing and duration of cycle-specific events cannot be determined from the analysis of the growth curve.
(i) synchronous growth experiments can be used to establish the presence of cycle-periodic events, but (ii) they cannot be used to establish timing and duration of these events.
the presence of a cycle-specific event is easily detectable in synchronous growth experiments, but that the timing and duration of the event cannot be accurately determined.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of mathematical modeling in the analysis of data derived from experiments on synchronous bacterial growth.
the development of a theoretical framework for the evaluation of experimental results obtained in synchronous cultures.
the development of a model of the cell cycle that will permit a quantitative analysis of the effects of environmental conditions on cell growth and division.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of cycle specificity was established.
the presence of cycle specificity in the component under study is demonstrated, but that its duration and timing are indeterminate.
a particular cellular event was present in the cycle and that it occurred at a given point in the cycle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of synchronous growth experiments for the study of cycle-specific phenomena is limited, and should be undertaken with caution.

, although the use of synchronous growth studies to assess the presence of cycle-dependent events is a reasonable approach, the timing and duration of these events are not easily established by such studies.
the results of synchronous experiments are not likely to provide a complete picture of cell-cycle-specific phenomena in bacteria.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in order to obtain reliable quantitative information on the timing and duration of cell-cycle events in synchronous growth studies, it is necessary to employ a rigorous statistical analysis of the data, and to consider the effects of experimental noise on the results.

, while synchronous growth experiments are useful in the detection of cycle-specific phenomena, the timing and duration of such events are best assessed using quantitative methods, and the use of qualitative analysis should be limited to the detection and confirmation of periodic phenomena.
, in the absence of an independent means of measuring the timing of cycle-specific events in the cell, the information that can be gleaned from synchronous growth experiments is severely limited.
